contract.proves:
A node removed from the cluster must take its etcd MEMBERSHIP with it.

SCAR — 2026-07-30, twice in one session, on the physical cluster.

globule-nuc was added to etcd during a Day-1 join and promoted to voter. Its
join then failed at a later phase (ScyllaDB), so the node was wiped. The wipe
did NOT remove its etcd member. The survivor was left with 2 registered voters
and only 1 alive:

    IS LEADER=false   ERRORS="etcdserver: no leader"
    raft index frozen; every etcd write hung

The whole control plane stalled behind it — 13.7s page loads, cluster-doctor
timing out — because gateway, controller and doctor all resolve config from
etcd. MemberRemove could not repair it either: that call itself needs quorum.
Recovery required restarting etcd with --force-new-cluster.

Two separate defects had to be fixed before the detach could work at all:

  1. step 0.3 of clean-node.sh was gated on `systemctl is-active
     globular-etcd`, and addressed only the LOCAL endpoint. A node is wiped
     after a FAILED join, and the join's own preflight stops etcd — so the
     guard was false in exactly the case the step exists for, and a dead local
     etcd cannot serve its own removal anyway.   (services ba418f39)

  2. it authenticated only with pki/issued/etcd/client.{crt,key}, which is
     materialised LATER in the join than the phase-2 service cert. A node that
     failed partway does not have it, so the step reported "TLS certs missing"
     and skipped.                                 (services b82bcbf9)

WHAT THIS ASSERTS — and why it is not the same as the existing
etcd-quorum-resilience scenario:

  stopping a member  → quorum requirement UNCHANGED (it is expected back)
  detaching a member → member list SHRINKS, so quorum requirement DROPS

That difference is the entire property. Here two of three etcd members are
decommissioned. Under correct behaviour the list shrinks 3 → 1 and the single
survivor still elects itself leader and accepts writes. With the pre-fix
clean-node the list would stay at 3 with 1 alive — quorum 2 unreachable, no
leader, writes hung.

The load-bearing assertion is etcd.write_test. Membership arithmetic can look
plausible while the cluster is actually wedged; a completed write is the only
proof that quorum is real.
